saying: Most commenters accept that specialist-versus-generalist use bears on risk but reject professional title as the test, urging risk turn on the gap between a function's knowledge domain and the intended user's ability to independently review outputs, validated through error-detection and escalation testing with the least specialized intended user. Cara AI adds a supervised non-clinical worker tier.

disagreement.text: Commenters split on whether user scope can be handled in labeling: some want the intended user's competency level stated in labeling and validated in that population, while others call labeling unenforceable and would credit only technically enforced access controls or workflow-embedded specialist review, assessing risk against foreseeable use.

sides.summary: Specify and validate intended user competency through labeling and intended-use statements.
Labeling cannot enforce user scope; credit only demonstrated technical controls or workflow embedding and judge risk against foreseeable off-label users.
